Consult Summary:
- 32-year-old woman (nurse) with 7 days of fever with alternating chills and sweats, diffuse myalgias, nausea, poor appetite, and fatigue; no focal symptoms; recently returned from rural and urban travel in Vietnam (4 weeks ago) despite daily malaria prophylaxis; plan for urgent in-person evaluation with malaria testing and blood work.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Persistent fever for ~7 days with hot/cold episodes and night sweats; generalized body aches; nausea with decreased oral intake; fatigue.
- Timeline:
  - Symptom onset: ~7 days prior to consult.
  - Course: Ongoing; OTC paracetamol/ibuprofen provide only partial, temporary relief.
  - Travel: Returned from Vietnam ~4 weeks ago after multi-week trip through rural countryside (trekking/cycling in farmland) and cities.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen (recommended doses) give slight, temporary improvement.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Night sweats; diffuse myalgias; nausea; fatigue; decreased appetite; reduced fluid intake; intermittent chills.
  - Negative: No cough, sore throat, cold symptoms, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, new or severe headache beyond her usual pattern, rash, joint swelling/tenderness (baseline back pain only), dysuria, urinary frequency, or urinary changes.
- Systems review (pertinent negatives as above).

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain:
  - Background: Attributed to prolonged sitting/poor posture; under active physiotherapy.
  - Complications: Not reported.
- Headaches/migraines:
  - Background: Longstanding; related to screen use and weather/pressure changes; no current change from baseline.
- No other major illnesses reported.
- Medications:
  - Paroxetine (Seroxat) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Ibuprofen — OTC; recommended dosing during this illness (specific dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Paracetamol (acetaminophen) — OTC; recommended dosing during this illness (specific dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Malaria prophylaxis during Vietnam trip — daily regimen; exact drug(s) unknown (patient recalls possibly taking an additional tablet on top of the first).
- Allergies:
  - Seasonal/pollen (hay fever).
  - No medication allergies reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse; up to date on vaccinations including Hepatitis B.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake.
- Exercise: Moderate physical activity a few times per week.
- Recent travel: Multi-week trip across Vietnam (rural farmland trekking/cycling and city visits); returned 4 weeks ago.
- Work impact: Currently struggling to work due to fatigue.

Family History:
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 68 (deceased).

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (teleconsultation). No vital signs provided.

Investigations:
- None completed yet.
- Planned per clinician:
  - Thick and thin blood films for malaria.
  - Inflammatory markers.
  - Additional “general blood tests” (unspecified) to be determined by examining clinician.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Febrile illness in a recent traveler (concern for malaria; no clear localizing source)
  - Assessment: 7 days of fever with chills/sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue without focal respiratory/urinary/GI symptoms; recent rural travel in Vietnam 4 weeks ago; took daily malaria prophylaxis but drug unknown. High suspicion for malaria; other travel-related infections possible. Needs in-person assessment to determine urgency and scope of testing.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent in-person evaluation today at central London clinic (or local A&E if clinic attendance is impractical).
    - Laboratory testing: Thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers; general blood tests as per examining clinician.
    - Work restriction: Not fit for work until evaluated and cause identified.
    - Triage/urgency: To be guided by in-person examination findings.
    - Administrative: Patient to call provided number to be booked; clinician to document plan for presentation at clinic/A&E.
- Issue 2: Nausea with reduced oral intake
  - Assessment: Likely related to underlying febrile illness; no red flags reported in transcript.
  - Plan: Acknowledge current OTC use with partial relief; further management to be determined after in-person assessment and labs.
- Issue 3: Chronic back pain (posture-related)
  - Assessment: Stable; under active physiotherapy.
  - Plan: Continue current physiotherapy (no changes discussed).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Malaria (likely Plasmodium species) — High likelihood
  - Reasoning: Rural travel in Vietnam; onset weeks after return; paroxysmal fevers with chills/sweats, myalgias, nausea; prophylaxis not fully protective. Testing (thick and thin films) planned.
- Enteric fever (typhoid/paratyphoid) — Moderate likelihood
  - Reasoning: Travel in SE Asia with potential varied food/water exposure; prolonged fever with few localizing symptoms. Lack of GI symptoms or rose spots noted but not exclusionary.
- Common viral syndrome (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) — Moderate likelihood
  - Reasoning: Systemic symptoms without focal bacterial source; occupational exposure as a nurse. Absence of respiratory symptoms and persistent night sweats are less typical but possible.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Vital signs and full physical examination.
  - Detailed medication list with doses, routes, and frequencies (including paroxetine and OTC agents).
  - Exact malaria prophylaxis regimen.
  - Pregnancy status.
  - Recent infectious screening/testing (e.g., COVID-19 test) not discussed.
  - Comprehensive travel exposure details (e.g., insect bites, freshwater exposure, food/water hygiene specifics) not fully elicited.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None of clinical significance noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor hesitations/filler words; no material omissions identified.
